final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is analytically useful but not sufficient to move to compliant_with_caveats. Under the policy, certification may proceed only if the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness is above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, but it also shows a material pharmacy prior-authorization regression for a named launch use case, stale prior approval, and only an informal monitoring note without approved acceptance. The Actor expressly concedes that the current record does not show an approved risk-acceptance artifact and does not show that the updated model card or release record is already completed. That means the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. The strongest supportable conclusion from admissible evidence is therefore that certification is not presently supported on the current record, even though a future caveated certification could become supportable if the required documentation is actually completed before launch.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card has been updated to reflect the current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows explicit disclosure of the pharmacy prior-authorization weakness for the named launch use case.
No approved risk-acceptance or reviewed mitigation artifact is in evidence.
Prior approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and do not satisfy the current-release policy predicates.
